Vision Elements is a computational-sciences consultancy. We solve the core, hard problems at the heart of very different domains: computer vision and 3D, medical and scientific imaging, signal and sensor processing, applied machine learning. Clients bring us problems that call for algorithmic depth outside their team's specialism; we reduce them to their mathematical essence and build the algorithm that works.
Who we're looking for
A junior with a real passion for math and physics, who lights up at a scientific challenge. Like us, you should be fascinated by the variety of problems, industries, and domains, seeing it as the best part of the job rather than chaos. Above all, you should enjoy the reduction: taking a messy, domain-specific problem and stripping it to its clean mathematical core. One month it's geometry and cameras, the next a biosignal or a reconstruction problem. We bring the domain context and mentorship; you bring rigor, curiosity, and the itch to make something actually work.
What you'll do
• Prototype algorithms for real client problems across imaging, vision, 3D, signals, and ML, from first principles to working code.

• Work shoulder-to-shoulder with senior scientists, learning how hard problems get scoped, de-risked, and delivered.

• The habit of thinking a problem through before coding it, and the discipline to verify results.

• Exposure to any of: deep learning, classical computer vision, DSP, medical imaging, 3D geometry, or numerical methods.

• A publication, thesis, or side project you're proud to walk us through.
• Comfort switching domains, with genuine excitement about doing so.
The engagement

Lynker is seeking a candidate to support the Office of Modeling and Development (OMD) of NWS in carrying out research and development work related forecast improvements for marine and seasonal forecasting. The candidate will perform job duties in a high-quality, independent, and collaborative way, developing and applying innovative methods for the primary work areas. The candidate will work with the UFS infrastructure in designing and evaluating the global coupled ensemble forecasting systems for long range forecasting. Development of global coupled Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models.
Development of marine (ocean and sea ice) forecast systems.
Development of subseasonal to seasonal probabilistic forecasting systems.
Development of AI/ML techniques for seasonal and marine forecasting systems.
Designing and conducting retrospective ensemble experiments and re-forecasts.
Exploring initial or analysis uncertainties, and/or model uncertainties (or model stochastic perturbations).
Analysis and evaluation of S2S probabilistic forecasts, and applications of multi-model ensembles and statistical post processing.

A Master or PhD’s Degree or equivalence in atmospheric sciences or meteorology, oceanic, mathematics, or related physical science with 1-2 years of experience in the area of global coupled ensemble forecast system development, sub-seasonal to seasonal prediction, numerical prediction, and/or AI/ML foundational prediction models. Advanced knowledge of S2S prediction and experience in developing ensemble based and coupled SFS for research and operational implementation.

Excellent knowledge and skills of modern programming languages and object-oriented languages, such as FORTRAN and Python.
Skills and knowledge of the High Performance Computing (HPC) environment with strong scripting capabilities.
Proficient with modern software development practices and version control software (e.g., Git and GitHub).
Demonstrated skill in communicating effectively with scientists of diverse backgrounds on technical details of the work plan and present results accurately and clearly in both oral and written form.
Ability to work independently on complex problems in a team and fast-paced environment and demonstrated skill in performing tasks requiring organization and attention to detail.
Ability to support team initiatives, demonstrate respect for team members, and seek team consensus.

Deep knowledge of ensemble strategy, reanalysis/reforecasting, and IC uncertainty.
Familiarity with operational NWP and/or an operational forecasting environment and experience with advanced technical workflows.
Experience with UFS applications and UFS infrastructure and knowledge of earth system modeling.
